package_info.package_name: mongose (example, applies to all listed typo-squatted packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typo-squatted clones of popular npm libraries, intentionally crafted to deceive developers into installing them. They contain additional code that exfiltrates all environment variables—including sensitive secrets such as passwords, API tokens, and credentials—to an attacker-controlled server (npm.hacktask.net) without user knowledge or consent. This direct exfiltration of secrets constitutes a severe security risk and is overtly malicious.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (code executes immediately when the package is imported or required, before any user code runs)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entrypoint of the package, ensuring execution on import)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read process.env if environment variables are set via files)
network (to send HTTP requests to external server)
environment_vars (to access all environment variables via process.env)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon import, the code collects all environment variables from the running process using process.env, serializes them as JSON, and sends them via an HTTP POST request to the attacker's server at npm.hacktask.net. This occurs automatically and without any user interaction or notification.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses all environment variables and transmits them to an external, hardcoded domain (npm.hacktask.net) without user consent or notification. This behavior is highly indicative of credential theft and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should never transmit environment variables or secrets to third-party servers, especially not automatically during import or initialization. Such actions violate user trust and standard security practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect limited, non-sensitive environment data for debugging, but only with explicit user consent and never the full set of environment variables. They also typically document this behavior and allow opt-out.
key_indicators: Direct access to process.env to collect all environment variables
Immediate HTTP POST request to a hardcoded, suspicious external domain (npm.hacktask.net)
Network exfiltration logic present in the main entrypoint (index.js), ensuring execution on import
No user notification, consent, or documentation of data collection
Code executes automatically on import, not as a result of explicit user action

attack_chain.action: A developer mistakenly installs a typo-squatted malicious package (e.g., mongose) instead of the legitimate one, due to the similar name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the developer's project.

attack_chain.action: When the malicious package is imported or required in the project, its main entrypoint (index.js) executes the embedded malicious code automatically.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code collects all environment variables from the running process.

attack_chain.action: The collected environment variables are serialized and sent via HTTP POST to the attacker's server (npm.hacktask.net) without user knowledge.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker receives sensitive secrets (such as passwords, API tokens, and credentials) from the victim's environment.

behavioral_signatures: Access to process.env and immediate serialization of all environment variables
HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, suspicious domains (e.g., npm.hacktask.net) during package import or initialization
Presence of code in the main entrypoint (index.js) that collects and transmits environment variables without user interaction
Network exfiltration logic that executes automatically on import
file_indicators: index.js or main entrypoint containing code that accesses process.env and sends data to external domains
References to npm.hacktask.net or similar attacker-controlled domains in source code
Unusual code patterns in entrypoint files that serialize and transmit environment variables
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to npm.hacktask.net (or similar suspicious domains) from development or CI environments
Unexpected network activity during package import or application startup, especially to unknown external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to scan npm packages for code that accesses process.env and transmits its contents to external servers, particularly in entrypoint files like index.js. Flag packages that reference suspicious domains (e.g., npm.hacktask.net) or that are typo-squatted versions of popular libraries. Monitor network traffic for HTTP POST requests to known attacker domains during package import or application startup. Combine these indicators to identify and block malicious packages before secrets are exfiltrated.
